source.cite: Fluke 6060A / 6060A-AF Synthesized Signal Generator Instruction Manual, Section 4A Performance Tests (printed pp. 4A-3 to 4A-17, PDF pages 119 to 133)
source.note: Points and limits from the rendered pages; leakage tests 4A-9 and 4A-10 are not built (owner). The 8902A replaces the counter, modulation analyzer, distortion analyzer and (4A-7, 4A-8) the power meter chain; 4A-5 and 4A-6 use the 96270A power-meter mode with a Rohde & Schwarz NRP40T (UNVERIFIED).

discrepancies: 4A-6 / 4A-7: introduction lists 120, 244, 245, 850, 1050 MHz; step a programs 30 MHz first. Introduction list used (owner decision 2026-10-28).
Figure 4A-3 section 1 prints "= +0.3" for -12.2 + 5.9 + 6 (= -0.3); the formulas are used.
Test 1 step e: counter limit "970 and 1030 kHz" is clearly Hz.
Table 4A-2 residual FM: "245 kHz to 512 MHz" for the 15 kHz band is clearly 245 MHz.
Test 8 step a: "4 MHz" is not in any frequency list; the level is not specified (+7 dBm used).
Unspecified levels: 4A-4 (preset -10 dBm), 4A-11 spurs A and B (+13 dBm), test 8 (+7 dBm).
4A-11 steps l.4 and l.5 give no offsets: read as absolute frequencies.
Test 6 steps f and j print the same 93 to 107 kHz limits with Option -651 (deviation 9.99 kHz): 9.3 to 10.7 kHz used for -651.

sections.title: 4A-3 Power-on test
sections.setup: Switch the 6060A POWER off, then on. The built-in self test runs (every indicator and display segment on for about 5 seconds). If it passes, the generator goes to the Instrument Preset state; if it fails, the failure codes appear in the four display fields (paragraph 4D-17).

flags: Prompt-based pass / fail: the self test is the generator's power-on test and has no remote result the manual confirms (SP02 / IT / SP11 are listed in Section 2 but not verified for this use). The reading is 1 for passed and 0 for failed.

sections.title: 4A-4 Synthesis test
sections.setup: Connect the 6060A rear 10 MHz IN/OUT to the 8902A 10 MHz time base input, REF INT/EXT switch to INT, and the RF OUTPUT to the 8902A RF INPUT (the 8902A replaces the frequency counter). The program presets the 6060A, programs 111.1111 MHz and a 111.1111 MHz frequency step, and set directly (not by the step keys), up to 999.9999 MHz.

flags: UNVERIFIED: 'one count' is taken as the 10 Hz resolution of the Table 4A-1 counter (the manual gives no Hz figure); the 8902A reads at 10 Hz resolution (7.1SP).
The level is not specified in 4A-4: the preset level (-10 dBm) is left unchanged (RF switched on).
Points 2 to 9 are n x 111.1111 MHz: the manual prints only 111.1111, 222.2222 and 999.9999 ("etc.").

sections.title: 4A-5 High-level accuracy test
sections.setup: Power sensor (Fluke 96270A in power-meter mode, R&S NRP40T) on the 6060A RF OUTPUT. The 6060A is preset and each attenuator section is selected with the levels of Figure 4A-2 (sections 4 to 7: -12 dBm then SP83 to SP86). Level errors, the eight section errors and their sum must not exceed +/-1.5 dB.

flags: UNVERIFIED: Rohde & Schwarz NRP40T on the 96270A power-meter mode (the 96270A manual never mentions NRP sensors).
Section 4 is selected with -12 dBm then SP83 ([SPCL][8][3]).
Section 5 is selected with -12 dBm then SP84 ([SPCL][8][4]).
Section 6 is selected with -12 dBm then SP85 ([SPCL][8][5]).
Section 7 is selected with -12 dBm then SP86 ([SPCL][8][6]).
Section 1 of the printed example (Figure 4A-3) shows +0.3 but -12.2 + 5.9 + 6 = -0.3: the formula is used, never the example.

sections.title: 4A-6 Mid-level accuracy test
sections.setup: Power sensor (96270A power-meter mode with the R&S NRP40T) on the RF OUTPUT. The sensor is zeroed with the 6060A RF off at each frequency. Levels -24 to -66 dBm in 6 dB steps.

flags: The manual's procedure (step a) programs 30 MHz first; its introduction lists 120 MHz: the introduction list is used (owner decision).
UNVERIFIED: whether the NRP40T range reaches -66 dBm (readings near the sensor floor may fail for that reason, not the generator).

sections.title: 4A-7 Low-level accuracy test
sections.setup: DEVIATION FROM THE PRINTED METHOD: the 8902A tuned RF level (as in 4A-8) measures -127 dBm instead of the power meter, 60 dB attenuator, wideband amplifier and spectrum analyzer.

flags: DEVIATION from the printed method (power meter + 60 dB attenuator + wideband amplifier + spectrum analyzer, steps e to h): measured with the 8902A tuned RF level, as in 4A-8 (owner request).
The manual's procedure (step a) programs 30 MHz first; its introduction lists 120 MHz: the introduction list is used (owner decision).

sections.title: 4A-8 Alternate-level accuracy test
sections.setup: 8902A with the 11722A sensor module on the RF OUTPUT; 6060A 10 MHz OUT to the 8902A time base input. Levels +11 to -127 dBm in 6 dB steps at six frequencies. Levels from -20 dBm up are read as RF power (M4); lower levels as tuned RF level (S4).

flags: The 24 levels are computed from "+11 dBm to -127 dBm in six dB steps" (the manual does not list them). The points run in an order that moves the sensor module once (all tuned-level points, then all RF-power points); the manual runs the levels in turn at each frequency.
UNVERIFIED: the switch from RF power (sensor module, 11722A) to tuned RF level at -20 dBm is this procedure's choice from the 8902A manual, not a 6060A manual statement.
UNVERIFIED: the sensor module's calibration-factor table must already be loaded in the 8902A (this program does not enter it).

sections.title: 4A-11 Harmonic and spurious test
sections.setup: UUT RF OUTPUT to the HP 8563E input (do not overload the analyzer). Harmonics are measured at +13 dBm; harmonics must be below -30 dBc, spurs below -60 dBc.

points.description: Harmonics 2 to 4 at 0.4 MHz, +13 dBm (worst, dBc)
flags: The 8563E has no remote harmonic function: the driver measures the fundamental and then each harmonic by software (CF / TS / MKPK HI). Analyzer settings are this procedure's choice (UNVERIFIED).

flags: Spur frequencies: "at the offsets of ..." (steps l.1 and l.2) are read as OFFSETS from the carrier (both sides, the worse is taken); every other "spur at ... MHz" (steps h, j, l.4, l.5, l.7) is read as an ABSOLUTE frequency. 1044.99 MHz = 244.99 + 800 MHz and 10 / 20 / 30 MHz are multiples of the 10 MHz reference, which is why they are not read as offsets. UNVERIFIED reading of the manual.

The level of spur checks A and B is not restated after step b: +13 dBm (still programmed) is used. The window, RBW and reference level of the analyzer are this procedure's choice; the reading is the highest peak in that window, so a spur hidden under the noise floor is reported as the floor level.

sections.title: 4A-12 Test 1: Internal modulation oscillator frequency
sections.setup: UUT RF OUTPUT to the 8902A RF INPUT, 10 MHz OUT to its time base. 90 % INT AM, +1 dBm, at the preset 300 MHz; the 8902A audio frequency counter reads the modulation frequency.

flags: Printed typo, corrected here: step e says the counter reads 970 to 1030 "kHz"; +/-3 % of 1 kHz (Table 4A-2) is 970 to 1030 Hz.
UNVERIFIED: the 8902A audio frequency counter (S1) replaces the frequency counter on the demodulated signal.

sections.title: 4A-12 Test 2: Internal AM accuracy
sections.setup: As test 1: mean AM depth = (+PEAK plus -PEAK)/2 (8902A detector D9, 50 Hz to 15 kHz), 90 % at 400 Hz and 1 kHz rate.

points.description: Mean AM depth, 90 % INT AM at 400 Hz, +1 dBm
flags: The 400 Hz point comes first, as left by test 1 (steps a and b); the frequency is the preset 300 MHz.
